tweets.body:
Proud to share the first results from Apex's automated AI research system.
We built it across the AI training stack:

— Smarter decisions before training: a new best suite mean of 0.8846 on SimpleTES/SLDBench.
— Better strategies during training: 0.892426 val_bpb on NanoChat Autoresearch, ahead of published results from Recursive and Tencent Hunyuan’s Hyra, and near the public SOTA.
— More efficient infrastructure underneath both: 1,036.1 μs on GPUMode TriMul H100, alongside new best throughput across all three MLS-Bench fused-attention configurations.

Across four benchmarks, the same system identifies what to improve, tests ideas, verifies the outcomes, and carries the evidence into the next cycle. Each result matters on its own; together, they show how AI research itself can begin to compound.
Read the full results and explore the artifacts below. We’d love to hear your thoughts and discuss where automated AI research could go next.

tweets.body:
I kept wondering: every AI benchmark tests whether models can follow a roadmap humans drew. What if we take the roadmap away?For many research-heavy tasks, how well does current LLM work? We built ASI-Bench to find out. 60 research tasks, 11 fields. Best agent scores 51.60 without human guidance. Open for contributions.

🌐 Submit a task: https://t.co/U6XFPbUbGp
📄 Paper (arXiv): https://t.co/efXOQ7kcGe
💬 Join our Discord: https://t.co/hdSxX45kRS
💻 GitHub: https://t.co/I5IXGvZpAV
If you find the benchmark useful, a Star ⭐ would mean a lot!

https://t.co/DDoiJEi0mP
https://t.co/AbJJCZw056
